title: 1 Samuel Chapter 26 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 1 Samuel chapter 26 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 1 Samuel Chapter 26 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 1 Samuel Chapter 26.

questions.question: Who came to Saul and told him about David's hiding place?
questions.correctAnswer: The Ziphites
questions.explanation: The Ziphites came unto Saul to Gibeah, saying, Doth not David hide himself in the hill of Hachilah (1 Samuel 26:1).

questions.question: How many chosen men did Saul take with him to seek David in the wilderness of Ziph?
questions.explanation: Saul arose, and went down to the wilderness of Ziph, having three thousand chosen men of Israel with him (1 Samuel 26:2).

questions.question: Where did Saul pitch his camp when seeking David?
questions.correctAnswer: Hill of Hachilah
questions.explanation: Saul pitched in the hill of Hachilah, which is before Jeshimon (1 Samuel 26:3).

questions.question: What did David do to confirm that Saul was indeed coming after him?
questions.correctAnswer: Sent out spies
questions.explanation: David therefore sent out spies, and understood that Saul was come in very deed (1 Samuel 26:4).

questions.question: Who was the captain of Saul's host that David saw with Saul?
questions.correctAnswer: Abner
questions.explanation: David beheld the place where Saul lay, and Abner the son of Ner, the captain of his host (1 Samuel 26:5).

questions.question: Who offered to go down with David to Saul's camp?
questions.correctAnswer: Abishai
questions.explanation: David asked who would go down with him, and Abishai said, I will go down with thee (1 Samuel 26:6).

questions.question: What was Saul doing when David and Abishai came to the camp by night?
questions.correctAnswer: Sleeping
questions.explanation: Behold, Saul lay sleeping within the trench (1 Samuel 26:7).

questions.question: What was stuck in the ground at Saul's bolster when he was sleeping?
questions.correctAnswer: A spear
questions.explanation: His spear stuck in the ground at his bolster (1 Samuel 26:7).

questions.question: What did Abishai want to do to Saul when they found him sleeping?
questions.correctAnswer: Smite him with the spear
questions.explanation: Abishai said, let me smite him with the spear even to the earth at once (1 Samuel 26:8).

questions.question: What was David's reason for not allowing Abishai to kill Saul?
options: He was afraid of the people
questions.correctAnswer: Saul was the LORD's anointed
questions.explanation: David said, Destroy him not: for who can stretch forth his hand against the LORD'S anointed, and be guiltless? (1 Samuel 26:9).

questions.question: True or False: Saul knew David's voice when David called out to him from the hill.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Saul knew David's voice, and said, Is this thy voice, my son David? (1 Samuel 26:17).

questions.question: True or False: David took Saul's spear and cruse of water while Saul and his men were awake.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: David took the spear and the cruse of water from Saul's bolster, and no man saw it, nor knew it, neither awaked: for they were all asleep (1 Samuel 26:12).

questions.question: True or False: David asked who would go down with him to Saul's camp before he sent out spies.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: David sent out spies first to understand Saul's coming (1 Samuel 26:4), and later asked who would go with him (1 Samuel 26:6).

questions.question: True or False: Saul returned to his place after blessing David and promising not to harm him.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Saul said, I will no more do thee harm... So David went on his way, and Saul returned to his place (1 Samuel 26:21,25).

questions.question: In 1 Samuel 26, which event happens first?
options: David and Abishai go to Saul's camp
David sends out spies to confirm Saul's location
Saul pitches at the hill of Hachilah
The Ziphites inform Saul about David's hiding place
questions.correctAnswer: The Ziphites inform Saul about David's hiding place
questions.explanation: First, the Ziphites came to Saul with information (26:1), then Saul arose and went to the wilderness (26:2), pitched his camp (26:3), and David sent out spies (26:4).

medium.title: 1 Samuel Chapter 26 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 1 Samuel Chapter 26 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to 1 Samuel 26:10, what does David say will happen to Saul in God's timing?
options: The LORD shall smite him, or his day shall come to die, or he shall perish in battle
Saul will reign forever as king
Saul will be forgiven and restored immediately
Saul will never face consequences for his actions
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD shall smite him, or his day shall come to die, or he shall perish in battle
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 26:10 states that David trusts the LORD to smite Saul or that Saul's day to die or perish in battle will come, showing David's faith in God's timing rather than taking matters into his own hands, as also emphasized in verses 9 and 11.

questions.question: What does David instruct Abishai to take from Saul’s camp after deciding not to harm Saul in 1 Samuel 26:11?
options: The spear and the cruse (jug) of water
questions.correctAnswer: The spear and the cruse (jug) of water
questions.explanation: In 1 Samuel 26:11, David forbids harming Saul but asks Abishai to take the spear and the cruse of water from Saul's bolster as evidence. This shows David’s respect for God’s anointed while still demonstrating his power to harm him.

questions.question: Why did no one in Saul’s camp wake up when David and Abishai took the spear and water, according to 1 Samuel 26:12?
options: Because a deep sleep from the LORD had fallen upon them
Because it was daytime and they were resting
Because David and Abishai were invisible
questions.correctAnswer: Because a deep sleep from the LORD had fallen upon them
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 26:12 explains that the people were all asleep due to a deep sleep sent by the LORD, enabling David and Abishai to take the items without being noticed, highlighting God’s protection over David and control over the situation.

questions.question: In 1 Samuel 26:14, how does Abner respond when David calls out to him?
options: He asks, 'Who art thou that criest to the king?'
He attacks David for disturbing the camp
He calls for Saul to wake up
questions.correctAnswer: He asks, 'Who art thou that criest to the king?'
questions.explanation: Abner’s question in 1 Samuel 26:14 shows his alertness and suspicion towards the unknown voice disturbing the king’s camp, setting the stage for David’s confrontation and appeal to Abner's integrity.

questions.question: What reason does David give Abner in 1 Samuel 26:15 for not protecting King Saul properly?
options: Because one of the people came to destroy the king
Because Abner was afraid to fight
Because Saul was hiding too well
Because David was stronger than Abner
questions.correctAnswer: Because one of the people came to destroy the king
questions.explanation: David accuses Abner in 1 Samuel 26:15 of failing to protect his lord, the king, when he says a person came into the camp to destroy Saul, highlighting the seriousness of Abner’s negligence in guarding God's anointed.

questions.question: According to 1 Samuel 26:16, what does David say about Abner and the others who failed to protect Saul?
options: They are worthy to die because they have not kept their master, the LORD’s anointed
They will be rewarded for their service
They acted wisely in hiding Saul
They will become kings after Saul
questions.correctAnswer: They are worthy to die because they have not kept their master, the LORD’s anointed
questions.explanation: David condemns Abner and his men in 1 Samuel 26:16 for failing to guard Saul, calling them worthy of death since they did not protect the LORD’s anointed, emphasizing the sacredness of God's appointed king.

questions.question: In 1 Samuel 26:17, how does Saul recognize David's voice?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 26:17 records that Saul knew David’s voice and called him 'my son David,' showing Saul’s recognition and perhaps a moment of tenderness toward David despite their conflict.

questions.question: What question does Saul ask David in 1 Samuel 26:18 regarding his pursuit of David?
options: Wherefore doth my lord thus pursue after his servant?
Will you be king after me?
Why did you steal my spear?
Are you ready to fight me?
questions.correctAnswer: Wherefore doth my lord thus pursue after his servant?
questions.explanation: In 1 Samuel 26:18, Saul asks a poignant question about why he is pursuing David so relentlessly, showing Saul’s confusion and possibly remorse about the pursuit, which David later addresses with humility and integrity.

questions.question: According to 1 Samuel 26:19, what does David suggest about those who have driven him out to serve other gods?
options: They are cursed before the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: They are cursed before the LORD
questions.explanation: David states in 1 Samuel 26:19 that those who have driven him out to serve other gods are cursed before the LORD, emphasizing his faithfulness to the true God and condemning idolatry or injustice against him.

questions.question: How does David describe Saul’s pursuit of him in 1 Samuel 26:20?
options: Like hunting a flea or a partridge in the mountains
Like a lion chasing a lamb
Like a mighty warrior seeking battle
Like a shepherd protecting his sheep
questions.correctAnswer: Like hunting a flea or a partridge in the mountains
questions.explanation: David uses similes in 1 Samuel 26:20 comparing Saul’s pursuit to hunting a flea or a partridge, illustrating the futility and triviality of Saul’s efforts against him, and demonstrating David's confidence in God's protection.

questions.question: What is Saul’s response after hearing David’s words in 1 Samuel 26:21?
options: He admits his sin and promises not to harm David again
He orders his men to capture David immediately
He calls for a great feast in David’s honor
questions.correctAnswer: He admits his sin and promises not to harm David again
questions.explanation: In 1 Samuel 26:21, Saul confesses he has sinned and tells David he will no longer harm him, acknowledging David’s value to him and showing a moment of repentance and humility.

questions.question: How does David demonstrate integrity in 1 Samuel 26:23 after Saul acknowledges his fault?
options: He says the LORD will reward righteousness and faithfulness and refuses to harm the LORD’s anointed
He demands Saul’s crown as a sign of submission
He mocks Saul for his foolishness
questions.correctAnswer: He says the LORD will reward righteousness and faithfulness and refuses to harm the LORD’s anointed
questions.explanation: David’s response in 1 Samuel 26:23 shows his commitment to righteousness and faithfulness, as he refuses to harm Saul even though he had the chance, underscoring his respect for God’s authority and moral integrity.

questions.question: What does David pray for concerning his own life in 1 Samuel 26:24?
options: That his life be precious in the eyes of the LORD and that God deliver him from all troubles
That he will become king immediately
That Saul will be struck down by God
That he will be forgotten by all
questions.correctAnswer: That his life be precious in the eyes of the LORD and that God deliver him from all troubles
questions.explanation: In 1 Samuel 26:24, David asks that as he valued Saul’s life, so God would value his and deliver him from tribulation, demonstrating humility, dependence on God, and faith in divine protection.

questions.question: What blessing does Saul give David in 1 Samuel 26:25 before David departs?
options: That David will do great things and continue to prevail
questions.correctAnswer: That David will do great things and continue to prevail
questions.explanation: Saul blesses David in 1 Samuel 26:25 by affirming that David will do great things and continue to prevail, recognizing David’s future success and God’s favor upon him despite Saul’s own kingship.

questions.question: Based on 1 Samuel 26:10-11, what does David's refusal to harm Saul teach us about Christian obedience and trust in God?
options: That we should trust God to handle judgment rather than taking revenge ourselves
That we should always take immediate action against enemies
That it is acceptable to harm those who oppose us when given the chance
That patience is unnecessary when confronting injustice
questions.correctAnswer: That we should trust God to handle judgment rather than taking revenge ourselves
questions.explanation: David’s choice in 1 Samuel 26:10-11 to not harm Saul, the LORD’s anointed, illustrates the Christian principle of trusting God’s timing and judgment rather than taking revenge, emphasizing obedience and humility before God’s sovereignty.

hard.title: 1 Samuel Chapter 26 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 1 Samuel Chapter 26.

questions.question: What accusation does David make against those who drove him out, in 1 Samuel 26:19?
options: They have cursed him before the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: They have cursed him before the LORD
questions.explanation: David says that those who drove him out are cursed before the LORD because they accused him of serving other gods, as stated in 1 Samuel 26:19.

questions.question: In 1 Samuel 26:20, what metaphor does David use to describe Saul’s pursuit of him?
questions.correctAnswer: Hunting a flea
questions.explanation: David compares Saul’s pursuit to hunting a flea, showing it as futile and insignificant, according to 1 Samuel 26:20.

questions.question: What is Saul's response after David confronts him with the king's spear in 1 Samuel 26:21?
options: He admits his sin and promises not to harm David again
He orders his men to arrest David
questions.correctAnswer: He admits his sin and promises not to harm David again
questions.explanation: Saul confesses his sin and tells David he will no longer harm him, as recorded in 1 Samuel 26:21.

questions.question: What does David ask one of the young men to do in 1 Samuel 26:22?
questions.correctAnswer: Fetch the king's spear
questions.explanation: David shows the king’s spear as proof and asks for it to be brought to him, according to 1 Samuel 26:22.

questions.question: According to 1 Samuel 26:23, why did David not stretch forth his hand against Saul?
options: Because Saul was the LORD’s anointed
questions.correctAnswer: Because Saul was the LORD’s anointed
questions.explanation: David refrained from harming Saul because he recognized him as the LORD’s anointed, as stated in 1 Samuel 26:23.

questions.question: What does David say about his own life in 1 Samuel 26:24?
options: Let it be precious in the eyes of the LORD as Saul’s was in his eyes
Let it be taken by Saul
Let it be surrendered to the people
questions.correctAnswer: Let it be precious in the eyes of the LORD as Saul’s was in his eyes
questions.explanation: David prays that his life will be valued by the LORD just as Saul’s life was valued by David, according to 1 Samuel 26:24.

questions.question: How does Saul bless David in 1 Samuel 26:25?
options: He blesses David to do great things and prevail
He curses David to never succeed
He sends David away with anger
questions.correctAnswer: He blesses David to do great things and prevail
questions.explanation: Saul blesses David, acknowledging his future success and prevailing, as recorded in 1 Samuel 26:25.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'cruse' (used in 1 Samuel 26:11) mean in the original text?
options: A small jar or vessel for water
questions.correctAnswer: A small jar or vessel for water
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word for 'cruse' refers to a small container or jar used for holding water, as seen in 1 Samuel 26:11.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used when David addresses Abner about his failure to protect Saul (1 Samuel 26:15-16)?
questions.correctAnswer: Chiasmus
questions.explanation: David’s speech in 1 Samuel 26:15-16 uses chiasmus, a literary device where ideas are presented and then repeated in reverse order to emphasize a point.

questions.question: Which earlier event in 1 Samuel parallels David sparing Saul’s life in chapter 26?
options: David sparing Saul’s life in the cave in 1 Samuel 24
David’s anointing by Samuel in 1 Samuel 16
Saul’s rejection as king in 1 Samuel 15
Jonathan’s covenant with David in 1 Samuel 18
questions.correctAnswer: David sparing Saul’s life in the cave in 1 Samuel 24
questions.explanation: David previously spared Saul’s life in a cave (1 Samuel 24), paralleling the mercy shown again in chapter 26.

questions.question: How does the theme of God’s sovereignty appear in 1 Samuel 26:23 in relation to the New Testament teaching in Romans 13:1?
options: Respect for God’s anointed authority is emphasized in both
Both focus on earthly power over divine
questions.correctAnswer: Respect for God’s anointed authority is emphasized in both
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 26:23 shows David’s respect for the LORD’s anointed, which aligns with Romans 13:1 teaching submission to governing authorities as established by God.

questions.question: What does David mean by saying 'the king of Israel is come out to seek a flea' in 1 Samuel 26:20?
options: Saul is pursuing something insignificant and elusive
Saul is hunting a great enemy
questions.correctAnswer: Saul is pursuing something insignificant and elusive
questions.explanation: David uses this metaphor to describe Saul’s futile pursuit as chasing something tiny and hard to catch, according to 1 Samuel 26:20.

questions.question: True or False: In 1 Samuel 26, David personally kills Saul during the night in the wilderness of Ziph.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: David spares Saul’s life and only takes his spear and water jug, as explained in 1 Samuel 26:9-11.

questions.question: True or False: In 1 Samuel 26:21, Saul admits he has sinned and acknowledges David’s precious regard for his soul.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Saul confesses his sin and recognizes David’s respect for his life in 1 Samuel 26:21.

questions.question: According to 1 Samuel 26:16, why are Abner and the men around Saul considered 'worthy to die'?
options: Because they failed to protect the LORD’S anointed king
questions.correctAnswer: Because they failed to protect the LORD’S anointed king
questions.explanation: David rebukes Abner and the men for not guarding Saul, the LORD’s anointed, making them worthy of death, as stated in 1 Samuel 26:16.

theological.title: 1 Samuel Chapter 26 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 1 Samuel Chapter 26 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does David's refusal to kill Saul, despite having the opportunity, primarily demonstrate about his understanding of God's authority?
options: David respected Saul as the LORD’S anointed
David lacked courage to kill Saul
David wanted to become king by other means
questions.correctAnswer: David respected Saul as the LORD’S anointed
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 26:9 and 26:11 show David forbidding the killing of Saul because he is the LORD’S anointed, demonstrating David's reverence for God's chosen king and God's authority over life and death.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is primarily illustrated by the deep sleep that fell upon Saul and his men while David took the spear and cruse of water?
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 26:12 reveals that the deep sleep came from the LORD, showing God's sovereign control over events to protect David and to fulfill His purposes without human interference.

questions.question: What theological doctrine can be drawn from David’s appeal that Saul’s blood not fall to the earth before the LORD, comparing the pursuit to hunting a flea or partridge?
questions.correctAnswer: Doctrine of Divine Justice
questions.explanation: In 1 Samuel 26:20, David contrasts Saul's pursuit with futile hunting imagery, pleading for justice recognizing God’s righteous judgment rather than human vengeance.

questions.question: How does David’s interaction with Abner and the people on the hill (verses 14-16) reflect the biblical principle concerning the protection of God’s anointed?
options: It shows the necessity of violent defense of kings
It emphasizes the accountability of those guarding God’s anointed
It encourages rebellion against corrupt leaders
It demands loyalty to military commanders over kings
questions.correctAnswer: It emphasizes the accountability of those guarding God’s anointed
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 26:15-16 rebukes Abner and the people for failing to protect Saul, God's anointed, establishing the principle that those entrusted with protecting God’s chosen must be faithful and accountable.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is highlighted in David’s confidence that the LORD will strike Saul or that his day will come to die, without David having to act prematurely?
questions.correctAnswer: Justice
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 26:10 shows David expressing faith in God’s just judgment, trusting that God will execute justice in His timing rather than David taking vengeance himself.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal teaching do 1 Samuel 26:9 and 1 Samuel 26:23 convey about the relationship between divine election and human righteousness?
options: Human righteousness can override divine election
Divine election demands respect and human righteousness in response
Human righteousness is unnecessary when divine election exists
questions.correctAnswer: Divine election demands respect and human righteousness in response
questions.explanation: Verses 9 and 23 teach that though Saul is divinely elected as LORD’S anointed, David’s righteousness is shown in his refusal to harm him, respecting God's choice and living faithfully.

questions.question: How does Saul’s admission of sin in 1 Samuel 26:21 contribute to our understanding of human repentance before God’s sovereignty?
options: Repentance is futile under God’s sovereign will
Repentance is a recognition of personal error before God's authority
Repentance is unnecessary when one is a king
questions.correctAnswer: Repentance is a recognition of personal error before God's authority
questions.explanation: In 1 Samuel 26:21, Saul confesses his sin and acknowledges David’s preciousness in his eyes, showing that repentance is an acknowledgment of personal failure under God’s sovereign judgment.

questions.question: What does the narrative arc in 1 Samuel 26 reveal about God’s providential preservation of David as a type of Christ?
options: David is preserved to show human kingship’s ultimate power
David’s preservation foreshadows Christ’s merciful restraint and protection
David’s survival reflects the weakness of God’s plan
David’s story is disconnected from the messianic hope
questions.correctAnswer: David’s preservation foreshadows Christ’s merciful restraint and protection
questions.explanation: David’s refusal to kill Saul, despite opportunity (1 Samuel 26:9-11), prefigures Christ’s merciful restraint and God’s providential protection of His anointed, linking David typologically to Christ.

questions.question: Which doctrinal insight arises from combining 1 Samuel 26:1-3 and 1 Samuel 26:12 about God’s providence in the life of His people during persecution?
options: God abandons His people during trials
God’s providence protects His chosen even amid enemies’ plots
Human planning is sufficient to avoid danger
God’s providence is unpredictable and random
questions.correctAnswer: God’s providence protects His chosen even amid enemies’ plots
questions.explanation: Verses 1-3 show Saul’s pursuit of David, while verse 12 reveals God’s providential protection by causing deep sleep on Saul’s camp, affirming God’s care amid persecution.

questions.question: What apologetic response does 1 Samuel 26:8-11 provide against the sceptical claim that David was merely politically motivated to kill Saul for power?
options: David was too weak to kill Saul
David’s refusal to kill Saul despite opportunity shows his respect for God’s anointed and trust in God's timing
David feared Saul’s army more than God
David wanted to delay killing Saul to gain more followers
questions.correctAnswer: David’s refusal to kill Saul despite opportunity shows his respect for God’s anointed and trust in God's timing
questions.explanation: Verses 8-11 demonstrate David’s moral choice not to kill Saul, revealing his reverence for God’s authority and refuting claims of mere political ambition.

questions.question: How does David’s statement in 1 Samuel 26:24 about valuing his life in the eyes of the LORD illustrate the doctrine of sanctification?
options: Sanctification is only about avoiding sin
Sanctification involves valuing life as precious before God and seeking deliverance from tribulation
Sanctification is unrelated to God’s deliverance
questions.correctAnswer: Sanctification involves valuing life as precious before God and seeking deliverance from tribulation
questions.explanation: David’s prayer in verse 24 highlights sanctification as recognizing one’s life as precious to God and desiring God’s deliverance from troubles, reflecting spiritual growth and dependence on God.

questions.question: What does the interaction between David and Saul in 1 Samuel 26:17-18 reveal about the nature of true repentance and reconciliation under God’s covenant?
options: Repentance requires immediate trust and confession
Repentance is unnecessary between a king and subject
Reconciliation depends on human effort alone
questions.correctAnswer: Repentance requires immediate trust and confession
questions.explanation: In verses 17-18, Saul acknowledges David’s voice and questions his pursuit motives, showing the beginning of repentance and the potential for reconciliation grounded in trust and confession before God.

questions.question: What theological truth is conveyed by David taking the spear and cruse of water from Saul’s bolster without waking anyone (1 Samuel 26:12) in contrast to human violence?
options: God endorses stealth and deception in war
God exercises control to prevent unnecessary bloodshed and allows restraint in conflict
God is indifferent to human conflict
questions.correctAnswer: God exercises control to prevent unnecessary bloodshed and allows restraint in conflict
questions.explanation: Verse 12 shows God’s intervention to keep Saul and his men asleep, preventing violence and highlighting divine control over human actions to avoid unjust killing.

questions.question: How does David’s rebuke of Abner in 1 Samuel 26:15-16 reveal the biblical principle of stewardship under divine authority?
options: Those entrusted with power must protect God’s anointed or face judgment
questions.correctAnswer: Those entrusted with power must protect God’s anointed or face judgment
questions.explanation: In verses 15-16, David accuses Abner of failing to guard Saul, emphasizing that stewardship involves responsibility under God’s authority and consequences for neglect.

questions.question: What combined teaching about human sin and divine mercy can be drawn from Saul’s confession in 1 Samuel 26:21 and David’s blessing in 1 Samuel 26:25?
options: Human sin leads to permanent rejection
Divine mercy allows restoration despite human failures, and God’s purposes prevail through His servants
Blessings are earned by human strength alone
questions.correctAnswer: Divine mercy allows restoration despite human failures, and God’s purposes prevail through His servants
questions.explanation: Saul’s confession of sin (verse 21) and David’s blessing (verse 25) together show that despite sin, God’s mercy can restore relationships and that God’s redemptive purposes continue through His chosen.
